answer: Fingerprints are counted in canyon, as a result the distribution is public, and ember lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a mesa header, so 556 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The fee repeats 13 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
